package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of urllib3 contain a denial of service (DoS) vulnerability in the _encode_invalid_chars method within util/url.py. The method's inefficient handling of percent-encoded characters allows an attacker to craft URLs that cause the function to consume excessive CPU resources, resulting in a DoS condition. While the vulnerability is not intentionally malicious, it can be exploited by attackers to disrupt service availability.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes user-supplied URLs by collecting all percent-encoded substrings into an array without deduplication, then iterates over each encoding in a nested loop to normalize them, resulting in O(n^2) CPU usage for specially crafted long URLs, which leads to denial of service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The method's quadratic time complexity for certain crafted inputs enables attackers to exhaust CPU resources with a single maliciously constructed URL, causing the application to become unresponsive.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal URL encoding should efficiently process user input and prevent user-controlled data from causing excessive resource consumption. In this case, user-supplied URLs can trigger expensive computation, violating performance and availability expectations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate URL encoding/decoding functions process percent-encoded characters, but should do so with linear or near-linear efficiency and should not allow user input to degrade system performance.
key_indicators: Quadratic (O(n^2)) CPU usage in _encode_invalid_chars when processing user-controlled input
Lack of deduplication of percent-encoded substrings in URL parsing
Ability to trigger CPU exhaustion with a single crafted HTTP request containing a long or repetitive percent-encoded URL

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted long URL with many percent-encoded substrings to an application using urllib3.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable _encode_invalid_chars method processes the input, consuming excessive CPU.

attack_chain.action: The application spends excessive time normalizing percent encodings, leading to resource exhaustion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Denial of service for legitimate users.

behavioral_signatures: Significant increase in CPU usage during URL parsing operations in applications using urllib3
Excessive processing time for HTTP requests containing long or repetitive percent-encoded substrings in the URL
file_indicators: util/url.py with _encode_invalid_chars implementation lacking deduplication of percent-encoded substrings
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with unusually long or repetitive percent-encoded substrings in the URL path or query string
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs and performance metrics for spikes in CPU usage or slow response times correlated with requests containing long percent-encoded URLs. Review code for inefficient handling of percent-encoded characters in URL parsing functions, specifically in urllib3 versions 1.25.2 through 1.25.7. Use software composition analysis or dependency scanning tools to identify vulnerable urllib3 versions in your environment and prioritize remediation.
